body:
It looks like the original PR for scala (#2409) noted that the module was likely to be a little on the slow side and said that scanning build files for scala versions would be a good future improvement:

> It may be possible to check project/build.properties but I believe it should be in a seperate PR that deals with the perf issues more thoroughly.

If you'd like to work on it, feel free!

Totally agree and want to add few ideas, that may or may not fit the high level design.

The `build.sbt` detection needs to be removed from both the Scala and Java modules, and handled by a new SBT module, right now versions are incorrect in context of SBT. 
Since SBT script(runner) manages SBT, Scala, Java versions by itself per project, it will be incompatible with the shell detection mechanism. SBT script version may be detected on a shell level, but in most cases the developer wants to see the SBT version of a project.
```
sbt --version
sbt version in this project: 1.5.7
sbt script version: 1.6.2
```
For better performance the project SBT version can be fetched from a file
```
cat build.properties
sbt.version=1.5.7
```
Scala version may be fetched by executing this slow command (and cache it inside the project directory?):
```
sbt "scalaVersion"
[info] 2.13.8
```
It will show a version for a singe-project SBT project. SBT also supports multi-project project with different Scala versions.
Another, faster option is searching the `build.sbt` file for strings like `scalaVersion := "2.13.8"`, but this may not work because of many reasons, for example receiving a version from a variable like `scalaVersion := scala212`.

Inside the a SBT project the detector may detect the language and show only the relevant versions in the prompt.
Since SBT follows the Maven directory structure it can be detected by checking directories existence.
```
src/main/scala
src/main/java
```

Another point that may confuse Scala developers is the Java version along side Scala version. Scala runs on JVM, when a Java version shown the developer may think it's a JVM version Scala running on, but it's not.
```
scala
Welcome to Scala 2.13.8 (OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM, Java 17.0.2).
```
